Title: Diagnosis of test `testSupplementaryUnescaping`

Details:
The test `testSupplementaryUnescaping` verifies if the `NumericEntityUnescaper` properly unescapes a numeric entity representing a supplementary Unicode character. The input is the numeric entity `𐰢`, and the expected output is the surrogate pair `\uD803\uDC22`.

Investigating the `NumericEntityUnescaper.translate(CharSequence input, int index, Writer out)` method reveals that it extracts the numeric part of the entity and parses it as an integer (either hexadecimal or decimal). Then, it writes the integer value directly as a character using `out.write(entityValue)`.

The issue arises because `entityValue` can represent a supplementary Unicode code point, which cannot be written directly as a single `char`. The method `Writer.write(int c)` writes the character corresponding to the single 16-bit UTF-16 unit, but supplementary characters require two UTF-16 units (a surrogate pair). Writing the integer value directly as a single character leads to incorrect output.

The test expects the unescaped string to contain a surrogate pair for the supplementary character, but the current implementation attempts to write it as a single UTF-16 character. This causes the test to fail because the output does not match the expected surrogate pair.

To correct this, the code needs to handle supplementary characters by converting the integer code point to a surrogate pair and writing both characters to the writer.

Suggested methods to fix:

org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaper.translate(java.lang.CharSequence, int, java.io.Writer)
